title: Chapter 54: Arts Activities Center
html:
Chen Ge kept his eyes fixed on the wooden chair in the middle of the corridor, mallet clenched in both hands. Ten seconds passed. The chair did not move.

Is it because I’m watching it?

He approached, switched on his phone’s camera, and wedged the device into the chain around the door. Then he retreated to the building’s neglected garden and waited.

The school lay unnaturally still at midnight. Not a bird called or an insect chirped. Three minutes later, Chen Ge returned to the dormitory prepared for the worst. The chair had not moved. It remained a meter beyond the broken ceiling light.

Didn’t move? What’s going on?

He retrieved the phone and reviewed the recording. Nothing unusual had happened; the chair had simply sat in the corridor.

It’ll only move when it’s around a living human?

The instant the thought occurred to him, unease prickled across his skin. He looked through the glass again. The chair had advanced another two meters and now stood terrifyingly close to the door.

It moved again. Why? If it only moves when I’m near, does it want something from me?

He was afraid—only a fool would not have been—but fear had long since stopped clouding his judgment.

The school is clearly haunted, but before I understand why, I should try my best to avoid these things.

His first impulse was to smash through the glass and reduce the chair to splinters. Too many corners inside lay beyond his view, however, and any one of them might conceal a threat. If he charged in, the chair might not be the thing that got broken.

Tonight’s mission is to find those red dancing shoes. As long as this strange phenomenon doesn’t interfere, I have no reason to engage with it.Chen Ge grabbed his phone and retreated from the door. I’d better search elsewhere first. I can always return if I don’t find the shoes. I only need to locate them before sunrise, and there’s still plenty of time.

After fixing the dormitory’s location in his memory, Chen Ge retraced his steps to the school gate. He switched off his phone and crouched nearby with the mallet ready.

Based on the time, the taxi behind me should have arrived already, so why is the road still so dark?

Headlights would have been impossible to miss in the absolute darkness, yet no light appeared on the road.

Could there have been an accident?

The other passenger still bothered him. He did not believe in coincidences; anyone coming to the academy at this hour had a reason.

Maybe whoever it is expected me to wait, so they got out early and walked the rest of the way. If so, this could be trouble.

He hoped he was wrong. Tonight was already dangerous enough.

Either way, I need to move faster. I have two advantages: I arrived first and learned the grounds, and Zhang Ya is on my side. She won’t let anyone bully me on her home turf, right?

Whether his eyes had adjusted or the change came from Yin Yang Vision, the darkness no longer seemed quite so impenetrable.

Those in the light open themselves to being hunted by those in the dark.

Keeping his phone dark, Chen Ge headed toward another building. The five-story teaching block was the tallest structure on campus. Behind it stretched an overgrown field, and beyond that stood an isolated building.

Its faded red paint distinguished it from everything around it.

The teaching block is only for classes, so the shoes probably aren’t there. The boys’ dormitory is even less likely. I’d better inspect the red building.

He skirted the field until he reached the strange building’s entrance.

It stood as tall as the girls’ dormitory but was only two-thirds as wide. Up close, its strangest feature was impossible to miss: a wooden sign before the door bore two words in red paint—NO ENTRY!

What is the purpose of this building?

The warning only sharpened his curiosity. Something must have happened here years ago. Maybe the red dancing shoes are inside.

He stepped around the sign and found the front door secured with two locks.

I could break down the door with the mallet, but the noise might attract whoever is following me.

Leaving the door alone, he circled the building and discovered a badly weathered window with a large section of glass missing.

There’s my way in.He reached through the gap and unlatched the window. To be safe, he waited several minutes for any sign of movement before climbing inside.

He closed the window and restored everything as best he could, then surveyed the room without lowering his guard. He had entered an art studio. Student work covered the walls, and plaster models lined the shelves.

This place looks creepy, but it can’t compete with my Haunted House.

He threaded between rows of plaster models and approached the rear door. Through its window, he saw a banner hanging in the corridor: ARTS ACTIVITIES CENTER.

Looks like I chose the right building.He eased the door open. Its long-neglected hinges released a shriek that scraped along his nerves.

Calm down, just leave immediately after you find the shoes.

Now that he was inside, he switched on his phone. Its dim light brought no comfort; if anything, it made the surrounding darkness more oppressive.

He checked the first-floor rooms one by one. All were art studios, some still holding abandoned easels and paintings.

This building has four stories; the dance studio I’m looking for is probably on another floor.

Phone in one hand and mallet in the other, Chen Ge climbed the stairs. A chill swept down his back as he reached the second floor.

A wooden chair waited in the corridor.

This thing again?

His hand tightened around the mallet.
